description:
Decided in defk-dtw.13. Add i16, i32, f32 as array element types (inputs and alloc/2), element types only, no narrow scalars. Reads widen as Elixir's bitstring match: i16/i32 -> i64, f32 -> f64 (exact). Writes: integers raise if out of range; f32 rounds to nearest as <<v::float-32-native>> does, raises if the rounded value is +-inf, underflow to 0.0 / subnormals follow Elixir. All float arithmetic stays f64. Native endianness. An input binary whose byte_size is not a multiple of the element width raises ArgumentError at the call. The unknown-type compile error lists the supported set. Elixir mode gets the same semantics. inf/NaN bit patterns in input arrays follow defk-q1c.
Done when: the semantics above have tests in both modes (incl. f32 fmax boundary, i16 +-32768 boundaries, bad-size binaries); max(min(v, 32767), -32768) stored into [i16] compiles with no write check (range facts) and vectorises like the hand C; docs/language.md documents the types and the caller-side bitstring forms.

comments.text: Per defk-q1c: [f32] reads use the on-read non-finite check (ArgumentError) and f32 writes feed the accumulated flag; see defk-i00.

Implemented on branch defk-4ai/element-types (3e9db87). Decisions: (1) an f32 write that rounds to +-inf raises ArgumentError 'value ... does not fit in f32', the same exception as the integer element range checks (reason :element_range in Defk.Test), not ArithmeticError: it is a limit on the store, not a float op. 'Feeds the accumulated flag' is done through the strip mechanism: defk_to_f32 is an nf helper (DEFK_NF_to_f32), so flat loops with f32 writes still run flagged and vectorise; the replay raises the ArgumentError at the first failing write. (2) [f32] input reads reuse defk_in_f64 on the widened value (NaN/inf survive float->double). (3) narrow integer writes (u8 too) drop defk_to_* when the value's lo/hi facts fit; unary minus of a literal now folds to a constant with facts (before, -32_768 was defk_neg_i64(32768) with no facts, so the clamp proved nothing). (4) Verified on arm64 clang: the PCM mix loop out[i] = max(min(a[i] + b[i], 32_767), -32_768) vectorises to the identical inner loop as hand C (4x sqadd.8h, width 8 x interleave 4). Bounds were proven with out = alloc(i16, len(a)) and i <- 0..(min(len(a), len(b)) - 1); with out = alloc(i16, n), n = min(...), the out[i] write keeps its bounds check because array length facts have no upper bound relative to other arrays (follow-up candidate). (5) Section 14 'Changes in flight' in docs/language.md left untouched; types documented in sections 3, 6, 7 and 12 directly.

title: Add [i16], [i32] and [f32] element types
